title: Data lake extracts INT-19 and INT-20 still listed as outbound adapters in FSD P2 v3, removed by Architecture v5
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1, A1.5, A2.6, A2.6.2 and the acceptance criteria of A2.6; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7, 8, 13, 16, 37, 43 and 44; Story Template and Rules v1 DP-17
section: FSD P2 v3 A1.5 outbound interface register, rows INT-19 and INT-20; BRD Program v4 section 5.2 still names the data lake and Power BI extract and the COLLINS feed
description: FSD P2 v3 builds and sends a nightly reporting extract to the data lake and Power BI (INT-19, JOB-15, 01:30) and a decision and outcome feed to COLLINS through the data lake (INT-20, JOB-13, 01:00). Architecture v5 states that the Workbench never connects to the data lake, that INT-19 and INT-20 are removed, that JOB-13 is continuous DecisionRecorded ingest in rwb-decision and that the reporting extract is built by rwb-reporting from its own projections. The two sources cannot both hold.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 7: Recovery adds services inside ACE's platform; it reads ACE data through views and never connects to the data lake. Slide 8: No data lake or Power BI connection (INT-19/20 removed). Slide 44: JOB-13 owner rwb-decision, mechanism continuous Kafka ingest; JOB-15 owner rwb-reporting, Airflow trigger, no data lake. FSD P2 v3 A1.5: INT-19 target data lake and Power BI, INT-20 target COLLINS through the data lake.
proposed: Architecture v5 wins under R-PREC rule 1. Legacy INT-19 is served as a delivery request from rwb-reporting through the rwb-integration delivery contract; legacy INT-20 is continuous ingest in rwb-decision. No lake target, lake file or lake delivery row appears in the PRD. BRD Program v4 section 5.2 needs the same correction in its next version.

title: FSD P2 v3 has the outbound file read the recovery.v_ace_* views directly; Architecture v5 and ADR-010 reserve the views to rwb-source-data
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 closing note, A2.1.3.1 BR-P2-001-ACE, A2.2.3.1 to A2.7.3.1, AC-ALT-P2-001-03; Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29 and 37; ADR-010; D-RCV-35 U4
section: FSD P2 v3 A1.5 and A2.1.3.1; BRD Program v4 REQ-DRI-006 and REQ-DRI-008
description: The FSD states that every outbound file reads ACE through the recovery.v_ace_* views, and its alternate criterion AC-ALT-P2-001-03 asserts that each addressee is read from v_ace_contact by contact_key. Architecture v5 states that only rwb-source-data reads the thirty views, that no other service holds a grant on the recovery schema, and that a change in ACE is absorbed in one place. A P2 read of the views would breach the service boundary.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 9: Only rwb-source-data reads the SQL views, so a change in ACE is absorbed in one place. Slide 29 and the Ownership Map: rwb_source_data holds the view contract; no P2 grant. FSD P2 v3 A1.5: An outbound file reads ACE through the recovery.v_ace_* views only.
proposed: The PRD requires every ACE fact an outbound file needs to be read through the rwb-source-data contract, one hop with a 2 s budget, and forbids any grant of rwb_integration on the recovery schema. The FSD wording stays as the legacy statement it is.

title: Job ownership of JOB-10, JOB-13 and JOB-15 differs between FSD P2 v3 and the Ownership Map
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 and A1.1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Jobs sheet; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 44
section: FSD P2 v3 A1.5 retry and exception column; BRD Program v4 section 5.2
description: FSD P2 v3 places JOB-10 (WIN notices, 16:00), JOB-13 (decision and outcome feed, 01:00) and JOB-15 (reporting extract, 01:30) inside P2. The Ownership Map places JOB-10 with P6 rwb-comms (AIRFLOW FILE WINDOW plus rwb-integration builds the file), JOB-13 with P7 rwb-decision (no Temporal Schedule, continuous ingest) and JOB-15 with P9 rwb-reporting. A schedule owned by P2 and a schedule owned by another service cannot both be true.
evidence: Ownership Map Jobs: JOB-10 P6, JOB-11 PLT, JOB-13 P7, JOB-15 P9. Arch v5 slide 44 rows JOB-10, JOB-13, JOB-15. FSD P2 v3 A1.5 lists JOB-10, JOB-13 and JOB-15 as the triggers of P2 interfaces.
proposed: The Ownership Map wins. The PRD names the owning service of each job and states that rwb-integration registers no Temporal Schedule and provides the delivery capability that the owning service calls.

title: Who retries a failed transfer is stated three ways: Airflow, the service retry ladder, or the outbox sender
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32 and 44; FSD P2 Integration v3 AC-EXC-P2-001-01 and A2.2; Story Template and Rules v1 DP-10
section: FSD P2 v3 A2.2 and A2.1.4.3; BRD Program v4 NFR-025 and NFR-026
description: Architecture v5 slide 32 states that rwb-integration builds the files and manifests and that Airflow owns the window, the transfer and the retry. FSD P2 v3 gives the service three attempts at 5 and 15 minute intervals and then an exception queue, and A2.2 gives the service the queue-and-retry duty. The two statements cover the same failure and assign it to different owners.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 32: rwb-integration still builds the files and manifests; Airflow owns the window, the transfer and the retry. FSD P2 v3 AC-EXC-P2-001-01: attempt 2 starts 5 minutes after attempt 1 and attempt 3 starts 15 minutes after attempt 2, then EXCEPTION. BRD NFR-026: three retries per item, then the exception queue.
proposed: The window, its opening time and the re-run of a window belong to the bank scheduler; the attempt ladder inside the window, the exception state and the owner task belong to the service. The PRD states both duties and leaves the single owner of a retry count to DL11.

title: FileDelivered and FileFailed have no row in the 31-row Ownership Map event register
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 43; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Events sheet
section: Arch v5 slide 43 additional events; Ownership Map Events rows EV-01 to EV-30
description: Architecture v5 gives rwb-integration the producer role of FileDelivered and FileFailed on rwb.integration.events.v1 as the two additions below the numbered catalogue. The Ownership Map Events sheet lists EV-01 to EV-30 and carries no row for either event, so the service PRD would have no owner row to cite for its own events.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 last row: FileDelivered, FileFailed, producer rwb-integration, topic rwb.integration.events.v1, consumers requesting service. Ownership Map Events sheet: 30 rows, none for FileDelivered or FileFailed.
proposed: The two events are P2's, keyed by case ID, with no numbered EV ID in the sources. The next Ownership Map version adds the two rows.

title: FSD P2 v3 builds the debt buyer tape from debt_sale_account, a table the Ownership Map gives to S6 rwb-debtsale
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 row INT-25 and AC-ALT-P2-001-03; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet; Story Template and Rules v1 DP-01
section: FSD P2 v3 A1.5 INT-25 built from column
description: The FSD says the INT-25 tape is built from debt_sale_account by account_key with account data from v_ace_account. The Ownership Map gives debt_sale_account to S6 rwb-debtsale and gives v_ace_account to P1 rwb-source-data, and DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables. P2 would hold a read grant on both under the FSD wording.
evidence: Ownership Map Tables: debt_sale_account owner S6 schema rwb_debtsale. Arch v5 slide 41: rwb-debtsale owns lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer. DP-01: never read another service's tables.
proposed: The tape rows and the account keys travel in the delivery request manifest raised by rwb-debtsale; the account facts are read through the rwb-source-data contract. P2 reads neither table.

title: Retry interval values differ between the FSD criterion and the interface configuration used by the service stories
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 AC-EXC-P2-001-01; story files of legacy RWB-E1-007 preconditions (interface version IF-2026.11); BRD Program v4 NFR-026
section: FSD P2 v3 A2.1.4.3 and A2.2; interface configuration rows INT-14 and INT-25
description: The FSD criterion fixes attempt 2 five minutes after attempt 1 and attempt 3 fifteen minutes after attempt 2. The interface configuration carried by the service stories holds max attempts 3 with retry intervals of 5, 15 and 45 minutes. With a limit of three attempts the 45 minute interval governs no attempt, so one of the two statements is unused or wrong.
evidence: FSD P2 v3 AC-EXC-P2-001-01: attempt 2 starts 5 minutes after attempt 1 and attempt 3 starts 15 minutes after attempt 2. Story preconditions: max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes.
proposed: The values stay interface configuration rows. The PRD states the FSD behaviour as the acceptance criterion and the row values as the configuration in force, and fixes neither as a product rule.

title: The FSD P2 requirement set does not cover the consumer-side composition slices assigned to rwb-integration in waves 2 to 4
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 Requirements served (REQ-DRI-006, 007, 008, 013 only); story files RWB-P2-E2002-CON, RWB-P2-E2007-CON, RWB-P2-E2033-CON, RWB-P2-E2036-CON and RWB-P2-E4046-APP; split_plan.json legacy entries with primary P2
section: FSD P2 v3 Requirements served; BRD Program v4 sections 5.2 and 5.3
description: The FSD P2 serves four requirements. The service story set also holds consumer-side contract slices for the ACE plan status, the booking confirmation, the composed case list, the queue write interface and the ALS settlement posting, whose requirements belong to rwb-case, rwb-treatment, rwb-payment and rwb-decision. A PRD that restates them as P2 product requirements would duplicate another module's baseline.
evidence: split_plan.json legacy: RWB-E2-001, E2-002, E2-003, E2-006, E2-007, E2-033, E2-034, E2-035 and E2-036 name P2 as primary and exist as P2 story files; the FSD P2 serves none of their requirements.
proposed: The PRD covers the P2-owning requirements and the one wave-2 orchestration step it traces to REQ-DRI-013. The consumer-side compositions stay with the owning module PRDs and are carried as open question Q-P2-06.

title: FSD P2 v3 keeps removed function and check IDs with no target behaviour
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.6 and A2.4; D-RCV-35 U1; Story Template and Rules v1 DP-17
section: FSD P2 v3 A1.6 functions removed by D-RCV-35
description: FEAT-DRI-09, the inbound half of FEAT-RDF-21 and FEAT-DRI-10, FileLoadAdapter, the DQ-057 and DQ-059 checks, the JOB-09 missing-file check and the interface_run and interface_signoff objects are marked removed with their later home. No target behaviour, state or acceptance criterion replaces them, and a reader of a product document cannot tell whether a removed row is still a requirement.
evidence: FSD P2 v3 A1.6 rows FEAT-DRI-09, FileLoadAdapter, DQ-057, DQ-059, JOB-09, interface_run, interface_signoff, all marked Removed by D-RCV-35 - later home: ACE ingestion.
proposed: The removed functions keep their IDs in an explicit exclusion table with their later home, and receive no FR, NFR or AC. The PRD states that no inbound adapter, inbound folder, inbound run or sign-off exists.

title: Neither BRD carries an approval record or a document status
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 document control table; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 document control table
section: Document control of BRD Program v4 and BRD Epic 1 v4
description: Both BRDs carry document, version, date, prepared by, release and structure, and no status field, no approval table and no Product Owner decision. The requirements approval gate therefore has no evidence in the source set.
evidence: BRD Program v4 lines 7 to 15 and BRD Epic 1 v4 lines 7 to 14: no status row, no approval table, no decision column.
proposed: The BRDs are taken as the business baseline and the PRD is issued as Draft with an empty approval table; the approval gate is recorded as open.

title: No non-functional target is stated for an outbound file itself: size, throughput, window length or volume per day
source: BRD Program v4 section 6.1 to 6.4; FSD P2 Integration v3 A2.1.1 metric table; Arch v5 slides 32 and 44
section: BRD Program v4 NFR-001 to NFR-027; FSD P2 v3 A2.1.1
description: The programme NFRs size the case store, the document hub and the decision log. Nothing states the largest WIN file, the number of notices in a file, the daily volume of the debt buyer tape, the length of the 16:00 window or the extract size at 01:30. The FSD gives one measure only, zero outbound items in the exception queue over one day.
evidence: FSD P2 v3 A2.1.1 metric table: one row, outbound items in the exception queue over one day, target zero. BRD Program v4 sections 6.1 to 6.4: no interface volume or window target.
proposed: The PRD inherits the programme targets that apply to every service and states the interface-level targets as open under DL11, with the placeholder of Template and Rules section R9.

title: The debt buyer tape is required to be masked before the data room, and to carry the personal data the sale terms allow
source: BRD Program v4 NFR-041 and NFR-039; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 row INT-25; BRD Program v4 section 6.7
section: BRD Program v4 section 6.7; FSD P2 v3 A1.5 INT-25 built from column
description: NFR-041 requires the debt sale data tape to be masked before it reaches the data room. The FSD builds the INT-25 tape for the buyer with personal data as the sale terms allow. Masking every field and allowing the sale terms to pass personal data cannot both be the rule, and no field-level masking rule is stated.
evidence: BRD NFR-041: The debt sale data tape is masked before it reaches the data room. FSD P2 v3 A1.5 INT-25: personal data as the sale terms allow.
proposed: The tape carries only the fields the sale terms and the approved mask list allow, and the mask list is a reference-data row owned by Compliance under DL26; the PRD states the rule and leaves the field list open.

title: The notification and logging rows of the FSD interface register state no Workbench behaviour
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 rows INT-17, INT-18 and INT-22; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7, 9 and 16
section: FSD P2 v3 A1.5 last three rows
description: INT-17 (NSS), INT-18 (LINE OA) and INT-22 (PII Kafka, audit and SOC logs) carry a retry and exception value of ACE and no adapter, trigger or state of their own. A product document cannot derive a requirement, an owner task or an acceptance criterion from them.
evidence: FSD P2 v3 A1.5: INT-17 and INT-18 adapter ACE notification path, retry ACE; INT-22 adapter ACE logging, retry ACE.
proposed: The three paths are stated as reused ACE capabilities with no P2 build and no FR, and the PRD records that their behaviour is ACE's.

title: FSD P2 v3 claims the transport of the partner portal and the document hub; Architecture v5 gives each its own service
source: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 scope statement and BRD Epic 1 v4 section 3.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 41; Ownership Map Services sheet
section: FSD P2 v3 A1.1 in scope; BRD Epic 1 v4 section 3.2 RWB-E1-007
description: The FSD says P2 uses the transport used by the partner portal and the document hub. Architecture v5 gives the partner portal to S9 rwb-partner and the document hub to P5 rwb-document, with their own contracts and their own transport, and gives P2 two party file interfaces only.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 16 rwb-integration OUT: WIN file INT-14 and debt buyer files INT-25 only. Slide 41: rwb-partner owns panel, partner users, instructions; rwb-document owns metadata, custody, retention.
proposed: The PRD states that the partner and document channels keep their own contracts and that P2 carries no requirement for them, with the FSD sentence recorded as superseded.

title: No retention period is set for an outbound item, a delivery record or the transmission evidence of a file
source: BRD Program v4 NFR-028, NFR-030, NFR-031 and section 6.5; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5
section: BRD Program v4 section 6.5; decision DL26
description: The retention classes exist for documents and for the decision log, and their periods are open under DL26. Nothing states how long an outbound item, an outbox delivery, a manifest or a transmission acknowledgement is kept, and a resend has to be provable after the case closes.
evidence: BRD NFR-028 and NFR-031: retention classes defined, periods not set, open under DL26. FSD P2 v3 A1.5: outbound runs recorded in outbound_item and outbox_delivery, no retention stated.
proposed: The PRD states the retention of P2 transmission records as open under DL26 with the section R9 placeholder, and requires only that a resend and its audit record outlive the retention period of the case they belong to.
